source: The same removed parking-lane footprint becomes a scar left by the old world's extraction, industry or defence.

variants.name: Destroyed crater
variants.atmosphere: The old road ends at a wound in the earth. Whatever struck here scattered the stone outward. A broad pool of lava surrounds an Ember altar at its centre; deep Crimson ore lies in the broken ground.
variants.storyConnection: A surviving scar of the fire that broke the world. Its cause stays uncertain; the exposed deep ore is the clue the player can carry away.
variants.layoutDescription: One complete impact bowl fits a broad usable pocket, avoiding buildings and holes. A continuous rock rim leaves an open approach; ellipse proportions stay within 2.5:1. Craters require at least 120 usable cells and a clear 9×9-cell patch.
variants.findsDescription: 1–2 finite Crimson ore deposits per site; this sample shows 2. No Sapphire scatter.
variants.hazardsDescription: A 5×5-cell lava pool surrounds the dry central Ember altar. Reaching the altar requires crossing hazardous lava; ore and the outside approach stay clear.
variants.guardsDescription: No fixed guards; the heat is the danger.
variants.lightingDescription: The central lava pool and Ember altar cast an orange-red glow.
variants.persistenceDescription: Mined ore stays exhausted. The central altar grants its usual daily boon; the lava remains hazardous.

variants.name: Abandoned quarry
variants.atmosphere: The crews who cut stone for the old kingdom's roads left in a hurry. Copper ore and unopened tool crates lie where the last shift dropped them, with ground spikes around the worked faces. Nothing here has been worked since the fire.
variants.storyConnection: The ordinary workers behind the ancient rulers' grand roads: their abandoned tools can now help the player mend what those roads connected.
variants.layoutDescription: An uneven worked rock face, a cleared loading yard, ground spikes and clusters of copper ore rocks. Repeating patches are 3×3 to 8×8 cells, separated by walking gaps.
variants.findsDescription: Up to two one-off Iron-pick crates per complete site. Each uses the existing gear reconciliation rule; opened crates stay empty. Copper ore rocks use normal mining.
variants.hazardsDescription: Visible ground spikes slow movement around the worked faces. The loading yard and approaches to crates stay clear.
variants.guardsDescription: No fixed guards: a quiet salvage site.
variants.persistenceDescription: Opened crates stay empty. Mined rock does not refill on the next visit.

variants.name: Strip mine
variants.atmosphere: The rulers wanted blue stone for their halls, and the hillside paid for it. Straight cuts march across the bare ground. Most of the wealth went away in carts; a few Sapphire seams still catch the light between the stripped benches.
variants.storyConnection: A landscape ravaged for the old ruling class's appetite for resources. Its relentless lines contrast with the living places the player restores.
variants.layoutDescription: Narrow intact benches follow the footprint’s long axis. Modules are 3 cells across and 3–8 cells long, with open cross-cuts and walking gaps. These compact modules suit small or skinny sites.
variants.findsDescription: Sapphire abundance reduced to one quarter of the previous vein rule. Remaining deposits are ordinary stone; small patches need not contain Sapphire. No bonus crates or buried hoard.
variants.hazardsDescription: No additional hazards: the damage is to the land itself.
variants.guardsDescription: Up to two splitting slimes per complete site; clipped edges use sparse cell-owned inhabitants without a finite site budget.
variants.lightingDescription: No special light source; Sapphire colour provides the visual accent.
variants.persistenceDescription: Deposits are finite, making each harvested bench feel worked out rather than endlessly replenished.

variants.name: Ruined stronghold
variants.atmosphere: Low square foundations are all that remain of the garrison that guarded the stone road. Goblins shelter behind the broken walls. Tier-2 chests and a few clay pots survive in the abandoned yards.
variants.storyConnection: The ancient ruling class's grip on the quarry and its road survives as a ruined military footprint, now occupied by scavengers. Crowns belong to those rulers; the religion's diamond remains a separate symbol.
variants.layoutDescription: Nominal 5×5-cell foundations keep readable L- or U-shaped wall fragments where buildings or site edges interrupt them. Surviving doorways remain open; guards, chests and clay pots use valid free ground.
variants.findsDescription: Up to three finite tier-2 chests per complete site, limited by fitting foundations. Some foundations also hold regular clay pots.
variants.hazardsDescription: Surviving doorways stay open; chests and clay pots use free ground inside the foundations.
variants.guardsDescription: Up to three goblins per complete site, using normal enemy eligibility and defeat persistence.
variants.lightingDescription: No special light source: a quiet, watchful ruin.
variants.persistenceDescription: Looted chests and defeated fixed guards stay cleared. Smashed clay pots stay smashed permanently. Foundation stones remain harvestable under the usual rock rules.
